question: What do we know about the generational wealth transfer, and how are these five preparing for it?

claims.text: Market size - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Cerulli projects households will transfer $123.7 trillion to heirs ($105 trillion) and charities ($18 trillion) between now and 2048. It puts Generation Xers' inheritance at $39 trillion and Millennials' at $46 trillion. It expects women in Baby Boomer and older generations to receive $40 trillion in 'horizontal' transfers, and women in younger generations to receive $47 trillion of the wealth transferred intergenerationally.

Market size - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Cerulli says most of the wealth owned by older generations will eventually be donated or passed to Gen X or Millennial heirs, an estimated $85 trillion. It says providers who can build relationships with these younger investors will be well-positioned.

Market size - UBS research (published 2026-04-22): UBS describes the Great Wealth Transfer as already in motion. It estimates USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades. Its introduction says USD 83 trillion is expected to pass between generations over the next two decades. The report is global; Cerulli's figures are for households, with a 2048 horizon. The two sources give different totals and time frames.

Client-side obstacles - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Cerulli's 2024 Private Wealth Management Executive Survey asked about the greatest challenges clients face in wealth transfer planning. The top-five factors shown are: not comfortable sharing financial information with children; fear children are not prepared to inherit; inexperience with multi-generational wealth strategies; clients unwilling to give up control; and worries about upsetting family members. The exhibit's percentages are 64%, 64%, 56%, 44% and 27%.

Wealth-transfer stance - Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-15), CEO Rick Wurster said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials. He said roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households. He said Schwab is well positioned to keep serving future generations when that wealth is passed on, and that its retention rate around wealth transfers is 'extremely high'. The 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15) shows ~70% of NTF retail households are Gen Z and Millennials, 80% of retail assets are held by U/HNW households, and ~75% of assets are retained in a wealth transfer event.

Wealth-transfer stance - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) lists competition for clients and personnel, in light of the evolving industry and generational wealth transfer and changing client demographics, among the Partnership's strategic risks. It says its ability to compete and adapt its business model may be adversely affected by generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations and demographics.

Wealth-transfer stance - Edward Jones, oldest to newest: The 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) says net new assets fell 10% from 2Q24, attributed to higher outflows. It cites an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm among the factors. The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) says net new assets fell 4% in the first nine months of 2025. It says outflows continue an increasing downward trend influenced by factors including an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm.

Preparation and capabilities - Schwab: The investor day deck (published 2026-05-14) lists Wealth Services offerings including Advisor ProDirect, Family Wealth Alliance, UHNW solutions and DAFgiving360. It frames them as delivering experiences that lead to deeper engagement beyond custody. The deck does not link them explicitly to wealth transfer. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says management estimates U.S. investable wealth exceeds $90 trillion, against Schwab's $13.08 trillion in client assets.

Preparation and capabilities - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership seeks to address strategic risks, including generational wealth transfer, through initiatives to deliver enhanced value for clients, colleagues and communities. It says it is continuing to make significant investments to attract and retain qualified talent. It also says it offers a competitive compensation program and benefits for financial advisors, CSTPs and home office associates. It names no specific wealth-transfer product or program.

Preparation and capabilities - Morgan Stanley: The strategic update deck (published 2026-01-15) lists, under 'Preserve Wealth', full-service wealth advice and asset allocation and family office solutions, trust and estate planning. It also lists Founders Wealth Strategies and Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits across client growth cycles. The deck does not call these a wealth-transfer response.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's GWIM segment press release (published 2026-01-14, period 2025-12-31) cites No. 1 on Forbes' Top Next Generation Advisors (2025) and No. 1 in Managed Personal Trust AUM. It also cites Best Private Bank for Philanthropic Services Globally.
adjacent.differs_because: This is GWIM segment recognition, covering both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank. It is not Merrill's own wealth-transfer statement or program, and it does not mention wealth transfer.

adjacent.text: Raymond James's RIA custody services page (page content as of 2026-07-12) lists 'Succession Planning and Acquisition' support and 'Wealth Strategies' for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes support for independent RIAs. The succession planning refers to the advisor's own practice, not client generational wealth transfer, and the page does not mention wealth transfer.

gaps.what: Wealth-transfer stance - Morgan Stanley: not found in the evidence provided.
